newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo and spot end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo and spot end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday mainly due to rises in the domestic A share market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 10.38 percent from 10.50 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover fell to 6.59 million lots from 7.78 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The continuing gains on the domestic A share markets both in Shanghai and Shenzhen encouraged some institutions to enter the market today, traders said.
"The early-maturing contracts bucked the trend (and fell), but they will rebound early next week with several new issues scheduled on the Shenzhen A share market," one trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up on rumours that the central bank would announce a cut in bank reserve ratios at the weekend, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in 2006 rose to 118.69 yuan from 118.08 yuan on Thursday. The turnover of the bond rose to 2.27 billion yuan from 0.41 billion.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose sharply to 3.42 million lots from 933,071 lots.
"The rumour that the central bank will cut bank reserve ratios during the weekend encouraged some institutions," one trader said. "It made turnover rise sharply."
Local analysts said technical charts indicated a clear upward trend, which might attract some speculators into the market in the next few days.
"The 121-yuan level seems to be the key resistance level of the 10-year bond in the mid-term," one analyst said.
